summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound and chronic indwelling Foley catheter use presented after a mechanical fall from her wheelchair, reporting lower back pain. Imaging of the thoracic and lumbar spine showed no definite fracture despite limited views. She was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by Escherichia coli, which was resistant to several antibiotics but sensitive to cefpodoxime. She was discharged on a 14-day course of cefpodoxime, along with tramadol, ibuprofen, acetaminophen, and a lidocaine patch for pain management. The patient was counseled on completing her antibiotic course and avoiding alcohol with tramadol. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to return if she developed fever, chills, or worsening symptoms.
